Questioned why the Airport Spur was not built when I-94 was built and for what the ramps at College Avenue were intended if not access to the airport.
Questioned what Grange Avenue was originally planned for.
Questioned why air cargo tonnage increase is not proportional to the increase in air passenger traffic?

When I-94 was being planned in the late 1960's, airport demand nationally was not high. Since that time, the rising population and its concentration in the been key factors accounting for steady increase in both passenger and cargo traffic. Milwaukee County has been striving to obtain approval for access to I-94 to service Mitchell Field since 1963.
College Avenue is designated as a County Trunk Highway and is intended to serve residential and industrial areas east and west of the ramps from I-94.
Grange Avenue was planned as a main east-west arterial for the City of Milwaukee.
The Airport Spur will carry both air passenger and air cargo. Air cargo is expected to increase 4.6 times from 47,500 tons in 1973 to 220,000 tons in 1990. Air passenger movements are projected to increase 2.6 times from 2,040,000 passengers in 1973 to 5,400,000 in 1990. Aircraft movement will increase 1.9 times from 254,000 movements in 1973 to 492,000 in 1990. Air cargo is carried in the bellyholds of the aircraft. Due to limited schedules that Mitchell Field can offer much air cargo is now being carried to O'Hare Field. Although aircraft flights are expected to double, greater air cargo capacities provided by these aircraft and fuller utilization of this capacity will result in a four fold increase.
